Saved data is used without checking its shape first.

terms.meaning: a request sent to an AI model service that returns generated text or data
a small save area inside the user's web browser that keeps data between visits
code that waits for a named signal, here careeros-skill-change, and then refreshes the screen

sections.name: File setup, LEVEL_ORDER
sections.title: Imports and skill level order
sections.what: Brings in React tools, the link component, shared page pieces, the storage helpers and the plan type. Fixes the four skill levels in order from novice to expert.
sections.why: Likely reason: the level buttons and the ordering need one fixed list.
sections.watch_out: The level names must match the names in saved data and in the style classes, or badges and buttons will misbehave.

sections.name: SkillProgressBar
sections.title: Progress bar
sections.what: Draws the coloured bar under each skill showing its percent, kept between zero and one hundred.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the bar from overflowing if a percent is out of range.
sections.watch_out: Only the width is kept in range. The colour is used as given.

sections.name: priorityColor
sections.title: Priority colour
sections.what: Picks the colour for a skill's priority: red for critical, orange for high, blue for medium and grey for anything else.
sections.why: Likely reason: colour gives a quick sense of urgency.
sections.watch_out: Unknown priority names silently fall back to grey.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 1)
sections.title: Page memory, loading and plan generation
sections.what: Keeps the page state and loads profile, applications, plan and progress from browser storage. It listens for progress changes. The generate action sends the profile and applications to the server and saves the reply, or shows the error.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page works from saved data and refreshes when a step changes elsewhere.
sections.watch_out: If the server reply has no data field, the save fails with an unclear error.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 2)
sections.title: Filters and summary totals
sections.what: Filters the skill list by priority or progress. Works out the totals for tracked, critical, in progress, completed and total weeks.
sections.why: Likely reason: the filter tabs and summary numbers need the same definitions.
sections.watch_out: Total weeks adds every skill's estimate regardless of progress, so it is the size of the whole plan.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage: if
sections.title: Loading and no-profile screens
sections.what: Shows a loading message until browser data is read, and a prompt to set up a profile when none exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: nothing useful can be shown until the profile is checked.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 4)
sections.title: Heading, plan summary and stats
sections.what: Shows the title, the generate or regenerate button, error messages, the no-plan prompt, the 90-day focus and the summary numbers. The done percent is completed skills divided by total skills.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the owner an overview before the detail.
sections.watch_out: The done percent counts only fully finished skills, so partial progress does not show there.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 5)
sections.title: Strengths, gaps and filter tabs
sections.what: Lists the top strengths and top gaps from the plan, then the filter buttons with their counts. The active filter is highlighted.
sections.why: Likely reason: strengths and gaps summarise the plan, and the tabs help narrow the list.
sections.watch_out: The tab counts and the stat numbers use the same definitions, so changing one changes both.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 6)
sections.title: Skill card header, level and bar
sections.what: Builds one card per skill with its name, category, priority, demand count, current and target level, percent done and bar. The percent shown is the higher of the plan's own figure and the completed-steps share.
sections.why: Likely reason: the plan's percent and the user's ticks can disagree, so the higher figure is shown.
sections.watch_out: Taking the higher figure can hide a drop if the saved plan's percent is stale.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 7)
sections.title: Evidence and learning path
sections.what: When a card is expanded, it shows evidence from the user's work and the ordered steps. Ticking a step toggles it and saves progress straight away.
sections.why: Likely reason: evidence explains why the skill is credited, and the steps are the plan to follow.
sections.watch_out: Each tick saves immediately; undoing means ticking the step again.

sections.name: SkillBuilderPage (part 8)
sections.title: Manual level override and collapse
sections.what: Lets the user set their own level for a skill from four buttons. The current level is highlighted. The expanded details close at the end of this block.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user may know their own level better than the plan does.
sections.watch_out: A manual level replaces the plan's level in the display until changed again, and it is saved in browser storage.

summary: Skill Builder page that turns the stored profile and job applications into a skill plan and tracks progress on each skill.
purpose: Shows which skills the user should build, their current and target level, and step-by-step learning paths the user can tick off.
why: Reason not stated in the code for keeping the plan in browser storage, beyond the use of the store helpers.
how: 1. Loads the profile, applications, saved plan and step progress from browser storage. 2. If there is no profile, shows a prompt to set one up. 3. The user generates a plan: the profile and applications go to `/api/skill-builder`, and the reply is saved. 4. The user filters skills by priority or progress. 5. Each skill card expands to show evidence and steps. Ticking a step or setting a manual level saves progress.
inputs: Profile, applications, saved plan, ticked steps, filter choices, and manual level choices. From the server, the plan returned by `/api/skill-builder`.
outputs: Skill cards, summary numbers, a saved plan and progress in browser storage, and error messages.
risks: The plan and progress live in browser storage, so clearing browser data erases them. The plan request sends the full profile and application list to the server, so privacy depends on that route (not visible here). Total weeks adds every skill's estimate, whatever the progress, which can look like remaining work.
debug: If no plan appears, read the error text, then the `/api/skill-builder` reply. If progress resets, check browser storage and the `careeros-skill-change` listener. If the page stays on LOADING, the browser-storage read may have failed. If filters look wrong, compare the saved completed steps with each learning path length.
